name: feature-pipeline
description: End-to-end feature pipeline: clone a repo, interactively brainstorm a spec and phased designs, then automatically align docs, produce plans, checkpoint-push the plans, record a branch-point test baseline, implement task-by-task (TDD), refine via the native ralph loop (gating on no NEW failures vs the baseline, with a stagnation backstop), and open a PR. Self-contained: all brainstorming/planning/execution processes are native template content with no external skill dependency.
author: arbitron

inputs.name: repo_url
inputs.description: GitHub repo URL to clone and work in.

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: Feature slug used for the branch name and docs. If empty, the branch uses a neutral 'feature' placeholder (never the repo name) and the real slug is resolved from the spec brainstorm for docs/templates.

inputs.name: spec_only
inputs.description: Stop after the planning package (spec + designs + plans) is produced, committed, and pushed — before implementation begins. The plans are checkpoint-pushed on both paths.

inputs.name: max_impl_iterations
inputs.description: Backstop cap on the draft-impl loop.

inputs.name: max_ralph_iterations
inputs.description: Backstop cap on the ralph refinement loop. A seam-based plan of N single-system areas and P paired reviews needs 2N+P passes MINIMUM with zero rework (one observed plan: 26 areas + 112 pairs = 164), and most areas need several passes, so 200 left almost no headroom.

inputs.name: no_progress_streak
inputs.description: Consecutive ralph passes that made no forward progress; the refine loop exits when this reaches 2 (stagnation backstop).

inputs.name: teams_webhook_url
inputs.description: Power Automate / Teams webhook URL for completion alerts. Leave empty in the committed sample (the notify-teams steps are no-ops when unset, or read ARBITRON_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL from the server env). The runtime workflow stores the real URL as this default.

inputs.name: resume
inputs.description: Resume an interrupted feature: detect which docs already exist for `slug` and skip forward to the first stage that still has work. Requires `slug`.

inputs.name: base_branch
inputs.description: Ref to base the feature worktree on (empty = the repo's default branch). init-workspace.sh already validates and shallow-clones this ref.

inputs.name: spec_path
inputs.description: Repo-relative path to the spec. Populated by the spec brainstorm on a fresh run, or by doc detection on a resume. Templates read {{spec_path}}.

inputs.name: resume_stage
inputs.description: Stage a resumed run enters at: spec | design | plans | implementation. Computed by detect-docs, never set by hand.

inputs.name: impl_blocked
inputs.description: Set by the impl loop when every remaining task is blocked. Routes the final terminal to done-blocked while still allowing the ralph loop and PR to run. Never set by hand.

nodes.label: Init workspace
nodes.description: Clone repo_url into {{workspace}}/src, derive slug + run_date, create the dev-<slug>-<run_date>-<instance-short-id> worktree at {{workspace}}/work. The instance-id suffix keeps branches unique across concurrent runs of the same repo/feature.

nodes.label: Promote vars
nodes.description: Lift init-workspace outputs to top-level vars for clean downstream references.

args: Feature pipeline started for {{slug}} on branch {{branch}} (repo {{repo_url}}).

nodes.label: Notify: started
nodes.description: In-app notification that the pipeline has started.

nodes.label: Brainstorm: spec
nodes.description: Interactive agent spec brainstorm; writes spec to disk and emits {slug, spec_path}.

nodes.label: Re-promote slug
nodes.description: After the spec brainstorm, promote the resolved slug AND spec_path to top-level vars so designs/plans/templates all use one consistent slug and one spec pointer.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push spec
nodes.description: Pushes the approved product spec commit. The spec brainstorm runs on a codex interactive_agent, whose sandbox pins sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=false — with codex's approval subsystem deleted that sandbox is the sole containment against a prompt-injected turn exfiltrating the worktree, so it must stay off. A git push from inside that turn therefore cannot work by design. The turn commits locally and this node, which runs outside the sandbox with the engine's auth env passthrough, does the push — also making the expensive interview survive a later crash instead of living only in the instance worktree. Note the codex agent_call path uses --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox and is NOT affected; this is specific to codex interactive_agent nodes.

nodes.label: Brainstorm: design
nodes.description: Interactive agent design brainstorm; writes design docs to disk and emits {slug, design_paths}.

nodes.label: Spec only?
nodes.description: Gate AFTER planning + checkpoint push: if spec_only, stop with the spec/designs/plans pushed; else continue to baseline capture and the implementation loop.

nodes.label: Align designs
nodes.description: Read spec + designs; fix alignment in place; commit.

nodes.label: Produce plans
nodes.description: Write detailed TDD task plans for each design phase; commit.

nodes.label: Align plans
nodes.description: Align spec+designs+plans; fix in place; commit.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push plans
nodes.description: Push the feature branch after the spec/design/plan phase so that expensive interactive+planning work survives a later crash/cancel/logout instead of living only in the instance worktree.

nodes.label: Capture test baseline
nodes.description: Before any implementation, detect and run the project's test suite(s) (mixed languages -> possibly several) and write {{workspace}}/test-baseline.json recording which tests already fail at the branch point.

nodes.label: Record baseline vars
nodes.description: Lift {{workspace}}/test-baseline.json into structured vars (test_baseline, test_commands, baseline_summary) so the ralph loop gates on NEW failures vs this baseline rather than a fully green suite.

nodes.label: Implement next task
nodes.description: Implement the next incomplete plan task, strict TDD, commit. Runs on a different model family than the planner that produced the plans and the approver that reviews the result, so no single family both writes and certifies the implementation.

nodes.label: Assess impl progress
nodes.description: Emit {all_tasks_complete, tasks_remaining, notes, all_remaining_blocked}. all_remaining_blocked is intentionally NOT in `required`: the claude-cli chat path has no native structured-output enforcement (schema is prompt prose only), so the model intermittently omits the key and a hard requirement kills the run. impl-gate only branches when it is true, so an absent value is correctly read as false.

nodes.label: Impl loop or exit
nodes.description: Exit when all tasks complete OR iteration cap reached; else loop.

nodes.label: Seed ralph files
nodes.description: Generate RALPH.md/focus-areas.md/gaps-identified.md; commit.

nodes.label: Refine (ralph pass)
nodes.description: Smallest correct improvement toward focus areas; run tests; update gaps; commit. Runs on a cheap high-volume model; it does NOT tick approval boxes — approve-area does, on a different model family, so no agent certifies its own change.

nodes.label: Record pass commit
nodes.description: Reads what the refinement pass actually committed (new commits since the previous pass, whether focus-areas.md / gaps-identified.md were touched) and emits progress_evidence. The assessor is toolless and used to score progress from {{refine.response}} alone — but the pass's Wrap Up asks it what REMAINS, so a compliant report structurally omits what it accomplished and the verdict became a coin flip that tripped the stagnation backstop on healthy runs. A commit is not a narrative. Never fails the run: no git evidence emits a conservative false and the assessor falls back to the pass's Progress: line.

nodes.label: Count review plan
nodes.description: Counts outstanding approval boxes in focus-areas.md and emits plan_complete, so loop termination is arithmetic rather than narrative. refine-assess is toolless: it could only read the pass's own <promise>FINIT</promise> claim and had no way to contradict it. Run ae3ec85f exited that way at pass 56 of a 200 cap with all 112 paired integration reviews untouched — 114 of 164 approvals outstanding — and shipped a PR whose review plan was 70% unexecuted. Fails closed: an unreadable plan emits plan_complete=false, and the stagnation backstop plus the cap still bound the run.

nodes.label: Assess refinement
nodes.description: Emit {done, notes, progressed, consecutive_no_progress}; done gates on no NEW failures vs the baseline (not a green suite), and consecutive_no_progress drives the stagnation exit.

nodes.label: Refine loop or exit
nodes.description: Exit ONLY on the iteration cap, a stagnation that survived its rescue pass (streak 3), or a review plan that is arithmetically complete AND regression-free AND assessed done. The cap wins outright; a streak of 2 buys exactly ONE stronger rescue pass per stagnation event; then plan_complete=false and new_failures>=1 each independently force another pass, so no verdict can end the loop while approval boxes are unticked or a regression is live.

nodes.label: Push & open PR
nodes.description: Push the feature branch and open a GitHub PR (auto-triggers the pr-review workflow on PR open).

args: Feature pipeline complete for {{slug}}: PR {{push-and-pr.pr_url}} opened. PR review will run on open.

nodes.label: Notify: PR opened
nodes.description: In-app notification that the PR is open.

nodes.label: Done (spec-only, terminal)
nodes.description: Terminal node for the --spec-only path.

nodes.label: Done (terminal)
nodes.description: Terminal node. Records final status so the walk ends cleanly.

args: Spec, phased designs, plans, implementation and the ralph refinement loop are done; a PR has been opened ({{push-and-pr.pr_url}}). PR review runs automatically on open.

nodes.label: Notify Teams (PR opened)
nodes.description: Rich completion alert to the Teams webhook after the PR is opened (no-op if teams_webhook_url unset).

args: Spec, phased designs and TDD task plans were produced, aligned and checkpoint-pushed. Stopped before implementation (spec_only).

nodes.label: Notify Teams (spec-only)
nodes.description: Rich alert to the Teams webhook on the spec-only stop (no-op if teams_webhook_url unset).

nodes.label: Assess plan dependencies
nodes.description: Gate: read the align-plans report and emit {has_unresolved, unresolved_count, gaps, notes} so unresolved producers are caught before implementation.

nodes.label: Deps blocking?
nodes.description: Proceed when nothing BLOCKS implementation (blocking_count 0 / has_blocking false) — non-blocking items such as externally-provisioned secrets no longer veto a run. Otherwise take exactly ONE interactive resolve pass; if a blocker survives it, stop. Two proceed conditions are checked because llm_call outputSchema is not enforced, so either field arriving well-formed is enough.

nodes.label: Resolve dependency (interactive)
nodes.description: Interactive opus-planner: point the human at each unresolved dependency, brainstorm the missing contract at implementation-design altitude, patch the blocked design/plan doc, commit; then loop back to re-align and re-check.

args: The planning phase could not close the dependency graph after {{max_deps_iterations}} interactive resolution passes. Implementation was NOT started, to avoid a livelock. Unresolved: {{deps-assess.notes}}

nodes.label: Notify Teams (planning blocked)
nodes.description: Escalation alert when unresolved plan dependencies remain after the resolution cap; the pipeline stops rather than shipping a plan the impl loop would livelock on.

args: The implementation loop stopped because every remaining task is blocked on a producer that does not exist and is outside its scope — a plan gap that slipped past the planning gate. Stopped rather than spinning to the iteration cap. Blocker: {{impl-assess.notes}}

nodes.label: Notify Teams (impl blocked)
nodes.description: Escalation alert when the impl loop detects all remaining tasks are blocked on non-existent producers; stop-and-escalate instead of spinning to the cap.

nodes.label: Done (blocked, terminal)
nodes.description: Terminal node for the escalation paths: planning or implementation stopped on an unresolvable dependency; a human must resolve the plan gap.

nodes.label: Resume?
nodes.description: resume=true routes to doc detection; otherwise the full pipeline runs from the spec brainstorm exactly as before.

nodes.label: Detect existing docs
nodes.description: Deterministic: globs docs/{specs,designs,plans}, normalizes filenames (strips ISO date + role suffix), token-scores against slug in both directions, and emits resume_stage + matched_slug + spec_path. A script, not an LLM: llm_call has no tools and its schema is not enforced.

nodes.label: Docs ambiguous?
nodes.description: True only when two different features score within 0.2 of each other, i.e. picking wrongly is plausible. The LLM tiebreaker runs ONLY in that case.

nodes.label: Disambiguate docs (tiebreak)
nodes.description: Picks which candidate feature the caller meant. It chooses ONLY the slug; stage and spec_path are recomputed deterministically afterwards by detect-docs-final, so a degenerate answer still yields correct routing.

nodes.label: Promote chosen slug
nodes.description: Lifts the tiebreaker's slug into the variable the detector reads.

nodes.label: Re-detect docs (chosen slug)
nodes.description: Second deterministic pass against the disambiguated slug. This is what makes the LLM advisory: the routing facts always come from the script.

nodes.label: Promote detected docs
nodes.description: Unambiguous path: adopt the detector results. slug comes from safe_slug, not matched_slug — matched_slug is empty when nothing matched, and adopting that would blank the slug and produce a placeholder branch with misnamed docs.

nodes.label: Promote detected docs (tiebroken)
nodes.description: Disambiguated path: adopt the re-detection results.

nodes.label: Resume at which stage?
nodes.description: The ladder: plans present -> re-align and re-validate them, then implement; spec+designs -> write plans; spec only -> design brainstorm; nothing found -> full pipeline. The implementation rung deliberately enters at align-plans rather than baseline-tests so a resumed run still passes the dependency gate (plans written by an earlier run were validated against an earlier repo state) and so spec_only remains meaningful on every resume path. Default is the full pipeline, so an unrecognised value costs time rather than skipping work.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push new plans
nodes.description: Pushes as soon as plans exist, BEFORE the dependency gate can route anywhere. Previously the only checkpoint sat on the gate's proceed edge, so a blocked exit discarded the entire spec+design+plan package when the workspace was garbage-collected.

nodes.label: Push before blocked exit
nodes.description: Terminal-path work preservation: both blocked escalations push the branch before ending, so a stopped run leaves its work on the remote instead of only in a workspace that is deleted on completion.

nodes.label: Mark implementation blocked
nodes.description: Records that the impl loop exited blocked, so the run still refines and opens a PR but is reported as blocked rather than complete.

nodes.label: Blocked or complete?
nodes.description: Chooses the terminal AFTER the PR is opened. A run whose implementation was blocked still refines and ships a PR, but must not report 'complete' -- that would assert verification it never performed.

nodes.label: Verify ralph seed
nodes.description: Greps the seeded RALPH.md for the loop protocol (both promise tags, Wrap Up, the stop-after-tag rule, one-issue-then-stop, no-backtrack) before the refinement loop consumes it. seed-ralph previously specified the charter content but not how a pass ENDS, so the agent improvised a protocol with no terminator and the loop ran without termination semantics. Fails fast rather than retrying: a deterministic grep will not pass on a second attempt.

nodes.label: Verify tests vs baseline
nodes.description: Deterministic regression gate for the refinement loop: runs the pre-detected suite(s) and diffs failures against the branch-point baseline. Nothing previously verified a pass's test claims — the agent that made the change also narrated the result, and refine-assess is toolless — so a regression introduced in pass N could be re-narrated as pre-existing in pass N+40 while every later pass built on it. Deliberately NOT placed in the impl loop: strict TDD makes a red suite the expected mid-task state there, so gating on it would reproduce the known impl livelock.

nodes.label: Approve area (independent)
nodes.description: The ONLY node permitted to tick an approval box, and a different model family from both the GPT implementer and the Flash refiner. Hard-blocked from approving while verify-tests reports any new failure or build break. The 2-approval redundancy assumed two independent judgements; with one profile doing both the fix and the approval it was the same model grading itself twice.

nodes.label: Refine (Opus rescue pass)
nodes.description: One stronger pass per stagnation event. Stagnation used to exit the loop and ship the PR with the review plan unfinished; with a cheaper worker that triggers more often. If the rescue also makes no progress the streak reaches 3 and the loop exits for real, so this cannot spin.
